Maintaining the 4.25–4.50% federal funds rate while capping QT more tightly (Treasuries runoff limited to $5B/month and excess MBS principal reinvested into Treasuries up to a $35B cap) reflects policy inertia consistent with Taylor-type guidelines and interest-rate smoothing documented by Goodfriend (1991, 1993) and Fuhrer (1996). The emphasis on “somewhat elevated” inflation and rising two‑sided risks fits a risk‑management approach under real‑time data uncertainty (Orphanides, 2001) and the classic Poole result favoring interest‑rate control when money‑demand shocks and uncertainty are material. Reaffirming the 2% target and attentiveness to expectations aligns with New Keynesian/DSGE insights (e.g., Lubik & Schorfheide, 2004) that policy must react persistently to inflation to ensure determinacy. Overall tone is balanced-to-cautious—solid growth and low unemployment offset by higher uncertainty and inflation concern—so sentiment is slightly positive rather than strongly upbeat.
